answer.worked: The sine wave has mean position $0$. Adding $3$ shifts it up by $3$, so its mean position is $3$.
The cosine wave has mean position $0$. Adding $3$ shifts it up by $3$, so its mean position is $3$.

Adding $\frac32$ shifts the sine wave up by $\frac32$ from mean position $0$, giving mean position $\frac32$.

answer.worked:
Let $u=2x$. The domain is $0\le u\le4\pi$.

$$\begin{align*}\sin u&=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\\u&=\frac{\pi}{3},\frac{2\pi}{3},\frac{7\pi}{3},\frac{8\pi}{3}\\x&=\frac{u}{2}\\x&=\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{3},\frac{7\pi}{6},\frac{4\pi}{3}\end{align*}$$

Let $u=x+\frac{\pi}{3}$. The domain is $\frac{\pi}{3}\le u\le\frac{7\pi}{3}$.

$$\begin{align*}\tan u&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\\u&=\frac{7\pi}{6},\frac{13\pi}{6}\\x&=u-\frac{\pi}{3}\\x&=\frac{5\pi}{6},\frac{11\pi}{6}\end{align*}$$

Let $u=3x$. The domain is $-3\pi\le u\le3\pi$.

$$\begin{align*}\sin u&=\frac12\\u&=-\frac{11\pi}{6},-\frac{7\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{6},\\&\qquad\frac{5\pi}{6},\frac{13\pi}{6},\frac{17\pi}{6}\\x&=\frac{u}{3}\\x&=-\frac{11\pi}{18},-\frac{7\pi}{18},\frac{\pi}{18},\\&\qquad\frac{5\pi}{18},\frac{13\pi}{18},\frac{17\pi}{18}\end{align*}$$

Let $u=2x+\frac{\pi}{3}$. The domain is $-\frac{5\pi}{3}\le u\le\frac{7\pi}{3}$.

$$\begin{align*}\cos u&=\frac12\\u&=-\frac{5\pi}{3},-\frac{\pi}{3},\frac{\pi}{3},\frac{5\pi}{3},\frac{7\pi}{3}\\x&=\frac{u-\pi/3}{2}\\x&=-\pi,-\frac{\pi}{3},0,\frac{2\pi}{3},\pi\end{align*}$$

Let $u=\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi}{3}$. The domain is $-\frac{\pi}{3}\le u\le\frac{2\pi}{3}$.

$$\begin{align*}\sin u&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\\u&=\frac{\pi}{4}\\x&=2\left(u+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\\x&=2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\\x&=\frac{7\pi}{6}\end{align*}$$

The function $f(t)=a\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}t\right)+b$ is drawn below, where $0\leq t\leq 48$.
The maximum value of $f(t)$ is $70\ 000$ when $t=12$.

What are the values of $a$ and $b$?

answer.short:
$a=30\ 000$, $b=40\ 000$

Use $\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=1$ at $t=12$ and $\sin\frac{3\pi}{2}=-1$ at $t=36$ to form two equations in $a$ and $b$.

At $t=12$, $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{24}\cdot 12\right)=\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=1$. At $t=36$, $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{24}\cdot 36\right)=\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)=-1$.
$$\begin{align*}
a+b &= 70\ 000 \\
-a+b &= 10\ 000
\end{align*}$$
Adding the equations:
$$\begin{align*}
2b &= 80\ 000 \\
b &= 40\ 000
\end{align*}$$
Substitute into $a+b=70\ 000$:
$$\begin{align*}
a+40\ 000 &= 70\ 000 \\
a &= 30\ 000
\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $a=30\ 000$ and $b=40\ 000$.

The curve shown below has equation $y = a\cos bx + c$ where $a$, $b$, $c$ are integers.
Find the values of $a$, $b$ and $c$.

answer.short:
$a=3$, $b=2$, $c=-1$

Use the maximum and minimum values to find $a$ and $c$, and the period to find $b$. Since cosine is even, $b=-2$ gives the same graph.
answer.worked:
From the graph, the maximum value is $2$ and the minimum value is $-4$.
$$\begin{align*}
|a| &= \frac{2-(-4)}{2} \\
&= 3
\end{align*}$$
Since the graph has a maximum at $x=0$, $a=3$.
$$\begin{align*}
c &= \frac{2+(-4)}{2} \\
&= -1
\end{align*}$$
The period of the graph is $\pi$.
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{2\pi}{|b|} &= \pi \\
|b| &= 2
\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=3$, $b=2$ and $c=-1$. (Because cosine is even, $b=-2$ also gives the same graph.)

content.prompt:
The function $g(x)=4\cos 2x$ is to be dilated horizontally by a factor of $\frac{1}{4}$ and then translated horizontally $\frac{\pi}{6}$ units to the right.
What is the equation of the transformed function $h(x)$?

$\text{A. }h(x)=4\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)$
$\text{B. }h(x)=4\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$
$\text{C. }h(x)=4\cos\left(8\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)$
$\text{D. }h(x)=4\cos\left(8x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$

answer.worked:
A horizontal dilation by a factor of $\frac{1}{4}$ replaces $x$ with $4x$. Then translating $\frac{\pi}{6}$ units to the right replaces $x$ with $x-\frac{\pi}{6}$.
$$\begin{align*}
f(x) &= g(4x) \\
&= 4\cos(8x) \\
h(x) &= f\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right) \\
&= 4\cos\left(8\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)
\end{align*}$$
Correct answer: C.

The depth of water in a bay rises and falls with the tide.
On a particular day the depth of the water, $d$ metres, can be modelled by the equation
$$d=1.3-0.6 \cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{25}t\right),$$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the depth of water at low tide and at high tide.

answer.short: Low tide $0.7$ m; high tide $1.9$ m.
answer.worked: Low tide is when $\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{25}t\right)=1$, so $d=1.3-0.6=0.7$ m. High tide is when $\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{25}t\right)=-1$, so $d=1.3+0.6=1.9$ m. The depth is $0.7$ m at low tide and $1.9$ m at high tide.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the time interval, in hours, between two successive low tides?

answer.worked:
The interval is one period.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Period}&=\frac{2\pi}{\frac{4\pi}{25}}\\&=\frac{50}{4}\\&=12.5\text{ hours}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: For how long between successive low tides will the depth of water be at least $1$ metre?

answer.short: $8\frac{1}{3}$ hours (8 hours 20 minutes). Solve $d=1$ and subtract the two times.
answer.worked:
Set $d=1$.
$$\begin{align*}1.3-0.6\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{25}t\right)&=1\\\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{25}t\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$
In one period, $\frac{4\pi}{25}t=\frac{\pi}{3}$ or $\frac{5\pi}{3}$, so $t_1=\frac{25}{12}$ and $t_2=\frac{125}{12}$. The depth is at least $1$ m between these times.
$$\begin{align*}\Delta t&=\frac{125}{12}-\frac{25}{12}\\&=\frac{100}{12}\\&=8\frac{1}{3}\text{ hours}\end{align*}$$
This is $8$ hours $20$ minutes.

content.prompt:
The graph is a function of the form $y = k\cos(a(x + b)) + c$.
Find the equation of the function.

answer.worked:
The maximum value is $3$ and the minimum value is $-1$, so:
$$\begin{align*}
k &= \frac{3 - (-1)}{2} \\
&= 2
\end{align*}$$
The centre line is:
$$\begin{align*}
y &= \frac{3 + (-1)}{2} \\
&= 1
\end{align*}$$
Therefore $c = 1$.
The period is $4\pi$, so:
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{2\pi}{a} &= 4\pi \\
a &= \frac{1}{2}
\end{align*}$$
The graph is shifted left by $\frac{\pi}{4}$, so $b = \frac{\pi}{4}$.
Therefore:
$$\begin{align*}
y &= 2\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}\left(x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right) + 1
\end{align*}$$

Syllabus Content
MAV-12-02 models, analyses and solves practical problems involving functions and their transformations

Transformations of trigonometric functions
• Use graphing applications to explore reflections, translations and dilations of, and confirm that the principles of transformations hold for, the trigonometric functions f(x) = sin x, f(x) = cos x and f(x) = tan x
• Apply the principles of transformations to graph transformations of the trigonometric functions f(x) = sin x, f(x) = cos x and f(x) = tan x, describe which transformations have been applied to y = f(x) and determine the domain, range, horizontal translation, vertical translation, dilation factor, period and amplitude when applicable
• Solve equations and graphical problems involving transformations of the trigonometric functions f(x) = sin x, f(x) = cos x or f(x) = tan x, using graphing applications or otherwise, within a specified domain

entries.description:
Vertical translations and mean position
The mean position is the average y-value of the wave.
• y = sin x and y = cos x have mean position 0.
• y = sin(x) + c and y = cos(x) + c have mean position c.
• y = tan x does not have a mean position.
• y = tan(x) + c shifts the graph vertically.

Vertical dilations and amplitude
• The amplitude of a wave is the distance from the mean position to the maximum value.
• y = sin x and y = cos x both have amplitude 1.
• y = k sin x and y = k cos x both have amplitude k.
• y = tan x does not have an amplitude.
• y = k tan x changes the steepness of the graph.

Horizontal dilations and period
The period of a wave function is the length of the smallest repeating unit.
• y = sin x and y = cos x both have period 2π.
• y = sin(ax) and y = cos(ax) both have period 2π/a.
• y = tan x has period π.
• y = tan(ax) has period π/a.

Horizontal translations and phase
The phase of a wave is the horizontal shift from the original position.
• y = sin x, y = cos x, y = tan x have phase 0.
• y = sin(x − b), y = cos(x − b), y = tan(x − b) have phase −b and shift right by b units.
